verdict.rationale: Intel's own material offers only a peak clock figure (up to 5.70 GHz), which is exactly the kind of slide number the story rejects. Independent reviews show the chip is competitive: faster than the 14900K in most tests and scoring about the same as the 9950X in one benchmark. But they also say AMD's 9950X leads in raw performance, and Windows single-thread performance consistency needed post-launch fixes from Intel, Microsoft and board makers. That makes the chip strong but not demonstrably leading. Missing for 10: an independent single-thread benchmark showing it leads competitors, consistent out-of-the-box single-thread performance on Windows, and hands-on evidence of instant interactive responsiveness.
